results.title: 'Essentially unusable': OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol to negative reception from AI power users
results.content:
Wharton professor Ethan Mollick had a more mixed experience with Astra. It built a playable space elevator in Blender and Unity, but he found the model “very uneven & weird” and harder to steer than rival models.

Astra now costs $8 per million uncached input tokens and $40 per million output tokens while GPT-6.2 Sol keeps its predecessor 6.1 Sol’s $2 input and $10 output rates. [...] Investor and former HyperWrite AI CEO Matt Shumer said he won't be releasing a longer written review as he has customarily done for other preceding OpenAI flagships. The new models "were essentially unusable,” Shumer wrote in a post on X. Developer and YouTuber Theo Browne also posted on X that 6.2 Astra was "the worst model OpenAI has ever released,” he wrote. They singled out the model's shortcomings in delegated work and creative tasks. [...] Dan Shipper, CEO of generative AI publication Every, said his team spent several weeks testing both models. He said Astra performed about as well as its predecessor on most of Every’s coding benchmarks, but often stopped early on end-to-end builds. He found that its push for brevity could make writing hard to follow or leave out necessary explanation.

results.title: GPT-6.2 Reviews: Why Testers Call Astra "Unusable"
results.content:
> OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol on 17 November 2026, and some of the best-known early testers panned them within hours. Matt Shumer called them "essentially unusable" and said he would not write a full review, Theo Browne called Astra "the worst model OpenAI has ever released", Ethan Mollick found it "very uneven & weird", and Every's Dan Shipper called it "a disappointing release compared to Fable 5.2". Sam Altman answered that OpenAI has "more work ahead of us on making the models [...] Early testers say GPT-6.2 Astra is hard to steer, stops too early, loops on long tasks and asks odd questions. Matt Shumer called the models essentially unusable, and Theo Browne called Astra the worst model OpenAI has ever released.

### What did Matt Shumer say about GPT-6.2?

On 17 November 2026 he wrote that he would not write a full review because he had a terrible experience testing GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, found them essentially unusable and does not recommend them. results.title: Since the Astra release, ChatGPT Pro has become increasingly unreliable for serious work - ChatGPT - OpenAI Developer Community
results.content:
The frustrating part is that Astra is actually very good.

Even Astra at Low can be extremely capable. For difficult autonomous work, it often performs better than what I am currently getting from 5.6 Sol.

The problem is that I cannot use it at the volume required for serious daily work.

I am already on Pro 20x, and I can still burn through the available usage in roughly a day when doing real development work. [...] That is an extremely frustrating position for a paying power user.

## GPT-6 Pro in normal Chat is also not usable for my coding workflow

Another major problem is GPT-6 Pro when working on coding tasks through remote desktop/RDC.

It repeatedly refuses or interrupts completely legitimate development tasks because of supposed safety restrictions.

What makes this especially frustrating is that I can take the exact same task, switch directly to GPT-5.6 Sol, and the work continues normally. [...] Since the Astra release, I have already purchased approximately 6,600 additional credits and reset my weekly limit eight times.

That is an absurd amount of additional capacity to have to consume just to maintain the workflow I had before.

So the current situation feels like this:

5.6 Sol has become too unreliable for the work I need it to do, while Astra is good enough to replace it but too heavily constrained to use continuously — even on the 20x plan.
